summary: André Bareau (1921–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the École normale d'Auteuil, Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France, supervised by Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at CNRS, EPHE, Collège de France, and Institut de civilisation indienne.

André Caquot (1923–2004) specialized in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and EPHE. He held posts at EPHE (~1955–1972), University of Strasbourg (1957–1960), University of Paris (1964–1968), and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture (b. 1945) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1969–1972), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1973–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1973–1977). He held a post at Laval University around 1979.

André Godard (1881–1965) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts (~1902–1909) and held a post at the University of Tehran (~1934–1949).

André Martinet (1908–1999) was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne and Humboldt University of Berlin under mentor Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938–1947), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1977).

André Mazon (1881–1967) worked in linguistics. He completed his studies at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1899–1903) and Charles University (~1904–1905), and later held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Swami Lakshman Joo, Louis Renou, Georg Morgenstierne, Alf Sommerfelt, and Olivier Lacombe. He held posts at Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and CNRS (1959, ~1964–1985).
André Wedemeyer (1875–1958) was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady and held an academic post at the University of Leipzig.

Andy Rotman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at CIHTS and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, among others. He has held posts at Smith College (attested 2013–2026) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Angela Falco Howard specializes in art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda. She held a professorship at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Angela Manderscheid works in Tibetology and related fields. She has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and at the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa, studying under Nalini Devdas, and held a post as assistant professor at Carleton University (attested 2008).

Angela Zito works in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1979–1989) and became an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University around 1996.

Philosopher Angelika Krebs (b. 1961) studied at Freiburg, Oxford, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, and Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt, and Basel (2001), with visiting positions at Freiburg, Zurich, Princeton, and Munich.

Angelika Malinar (b. 1961) works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Tübingen, and has held posts at the Free University of Berlin, SOAS University of London, and the University of Zurich.

Angelo Brelich (1913–1977) was a scholar in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Erzsébet University (~1932–1937) and subsequently held an academic post at Sapienza University of Rome (~1958–1977).

Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).
Anil Kumar works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Hyderabad by 2012 and holds a post at the same institution.

Anil Vidyalankar (b. 1928) is a scholar in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi. He founded Sandhaan in 1988, serving as its director (attested 1999).

Anirban Dash works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a post as a research assistant (attested 2003–2005) and later as an associate professor of Sanskrit (attested 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
